conflicts.point: Whether point-of-deployment market-access gating effectively prevents dangerous model proliferation or merely establishes a private corporate surveillance and censorship mechanism.

positions.stance: Point-of-access gating bypasses headcount limits by compelling cloud providers and app stores to verify compliance manifests before executing weights.
Gating the market replaces state border guards with private platform censors and fails to stop peer-to-peer offshore weight transfers.

verdicts.conflict: Whether point-of-deployment market-access gating effectively prevents dangerous model proliferation or merely establishes a private corporate surveillance and censorship mechanism.
verdicts.rationale: Both positions rely on unproven assertions about future compliance behaviors across cloud providers and peer-to-peer networks. Neither camp provides empirical proof regarding whether market-access gating can successfully intercept illicit weight transfers without creating private monopolies.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Real-world data from pilot programs enforcing compute thresholds via cloud providers, specifically measuring both illicit weight leakage rates and the market concentration effects on smaller developers.
